# mapbox geocoder

Geocoding v6 API

The **Mapbox Geocoding API** does two things: _forward geocoding_ and _reverse geocoding_:

3 commands. A description too long for its table cell is shortened here; `mapbox --schema <command>` has the whole of every one, as JSON. Placeholders in the examples are written in `UPPER_CASE` and have to be replaced.

## Commands

### mapbox geocoder batch

Batch geocoding

The batch geocoding query type allows you to request up to 50 forward or reverse geocoding queries in a single request.

Batch geocoding requests are formatted as a JSON array passed as the `BODY` of the request, with multiple search queries one after another. Fields which were defined as query parameters in the URL string will become fields in the JSON object. Fields specifying multiple values (for example `types`, `country`, `bbox`, `proximity`) can be passed either as comma-separated strings or as JSON-formatted arrays (for example a types filter value could be represented as `"address,street,place"` or `["address", "street", "place"]`).

In a single batch geocoding request, you can bundle queries of different types, including forward queries, forward Structured Input queries, and reverse queries. Each query can also have parameters defined individually — for example one query could have IP proximity set to on while the rest have it off.

<Note title="Billing for batch geocoding requests">
  Each individual search in a batch geocoding request counts as one request.
</Note>

#### Example request: Batch geocoding

```bash
curl --location --request POST "https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/batch?access_token=YOUR_MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '[
    {
        "types": ["address"],
        "q": "1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20500, United States",
        "bbox": [-80, 35, -70, 40],
        "limit": 1
    },
    {
        "country": "us",
        "address_number": "1600",
        "street": "Pennsylvania Avenue NW",
        "postcode": "20500",
        "place": "Washington, DC"
    },
    {
        "types": ["address"],
        "longitude": -73.986136,
        "latitude": 40.748895
    }
]'
```

#### Response: Batch geocoding

The response from a batch geocoding query is an object with a `batch` property. The batch property is an array of Geocoding response objects. The order of queries in the request determines the order of corresponding objects in the batch array. If there are no results returned for a particular query within the batch, the `features` array for that query is empty (`"features": []`).

```json
{
  "batch": [
    {
      "type": "FeatureCollection",
      "features": [
        {
          "type": "Feature",
          "id": "dXJuOm1ieGFkcjo2YzdhYjM4Yi05YzM4LTQ3ZDItODFkMS1jYzZlYjg5YzliMWM",
          "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [-77.03655, 38.89768] },
          "properties": {
            "mapbox_id": "dXJuOm1ieGFkcjo2YzdhYjM4Yi05YzM4LTQ3ZDItODFkMS1jYzZlYjg5YzliMWM",
            "feature_type": "address",
            "name": "1600 Pennsylvania Avenue Northwest",
            "coordinates": { "longitude": -77.03655, "latitude": 38.89768, "accuracy": "rooftop" },
            "place_formatted": "Washington, District of Columbia 20500, United States",
            "match_code": {
              "address_number": "matched", "street": "matched", "postcode": "matched",
              "place": "matched", "region": "matched", "locality": "not_applicable",
              "country": "inferred", "confidence": "exact"
            }
          }
        }
      ],
      "attribution": "NOTICE: © 2023 Mapbox and its suppliers. All rights reserved. Use of this data is subject to the Mapbox Terms of Service (https://www.mapbox.com/about/maps/). This response and the information it contains may not be retained."
    },
    {
      "type": "FeatureCollection",
      "features": [],
      "attribution": "NOTICE: © 2023 Mapbox and its suppliers. All rights reserved. Use of this data is subject to the Mapbox Terms of Service (https://www.mapbox.com/about/maps/). This response and the information it contains may not be retained."

          "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [-73.9861365, 40.7488949] },
          "properties": {
            "mapbox_id": "dXJuOm1ieGFkcjplMzVmMzZiOC1kYjRmLTQyOWItOWE4ZC0yZGQ3ZmQ1OTUzMTY",
```

`POST https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/batch`

| Argument | Written as | Required | Type | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `--data DATA` `-d` | yes | string |  | Request body as a JSON string, or `@<path>` to read a file and `@-` to read stdin. Sent in the request body. Sent as `application/json`. |
| `dry-run` | `--dry-run` | no | boolean |  | Print the request this would send, then exit without sending it. |
| `permanent` | `--permanent` | no | boolean |  | Specify whether you intend to store the results of the query (`true`) or not (`false`, default). Sent in the request query. |

```sh
mapbox geocoder batch --data '{}'
```

### mapbox geocoder forward

Forward geocoding

The **forward geocoding** query type allows you to look up a location using a string of search text and returns its standardized address, geographic context, and coordinates.

#### Forward geocoding with search text input

Use the `q` parameter to search with a string of text. The search text should be expressed as a URL-encoded UTF-8 string, and must not contain the semicolon character (either raw or URL-encoded). Your search text, once decoded, must consist of at most 20 words and numbers separated by spacing and punctuation, and at most 256 characters.

The accuracy of coordinates returned by a forward geocoding request can be affected by how the addresses in the query are formatted. Learn more about address formatting best practices in the [Address geocoding format guide](https://docs.mapbox.com/help/troubleshooting/address-geocoding-format-guide/).


#### Forward geocoding with structured input

**Structured Input** is a type of forward geocoding search that allows you to define the feature type of each element of the search query by type. This can increase the accuracy of results for well-formed datasets. To use Structured Input, the `q` parameter is dropped in favor of separate parameters for each feature type: `address_line1`, `address_number`, `street`, `block`, `place`, `region`, `postcode`, `locality`, `neighborhood`, `country`.

For best results, each element of the query must be assigned a feature type, and set `autocomplete` to `false`.

For the `country` structured input parameter specifically: when the ISO code is passed it acts as a hard filter on search results; when a full country name is passed, it influences the search results but is not a hard filter.

#### Recommended testing method for entrance data

Run an offline comparison of entrance data to test it quickly at scale:

1. Run existing geocoder locations and Mapbox entrance points against the same set of addresses.
2. Compare each result to a known reference point (for example, a past delivery location or other ground-truth coordinate) and measure which point is closer to the reference.
3. The resulting distance-to-reference metric quantifies how often Mapbox entrance data places drivers closer to the correct entrance. The metric can be directly correlated to the efficiency gains, reduced dwell time, and lower support volume that would result from deploying Mapbox entrance locations in a production environment.

#### Intersection search support

Intersection search allows users to search for a point where two streets intersect, without a precise address. Make an intersection search request by inserting an intersection connector between 2 streets. Intersection search is not available in all countries.

| Connector    | Applicable countries                                 |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `&`          | All countries where intersection search is supported |
| `and` or `x` | IN, JM, US                                           |
| `e`          | AR, BO, BR, CO, CR, DO, EC, GT, NI, PA, PE, SV, UY  |

```bash
# Intersection search using 'and'
$ curl "https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/forward?q=Market%20Street%20and%20Fremont%20Street&proximity=-122.39738575285674,37.7925147111369453&access_token=YOUR_MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN"

# Intersection search using '&'
$ curl "https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/forward?q=Market%20Street%20%26%20Fremont%20Street&proximity=-122.39738575285674,37.7925147111369453&access_token=YOUR_MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

`GET https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/forward`

| Argument | Written as | Required | Type | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `address-line1` | `--address-line1 ADDRESS_LINE1` | no | string |  | Structured input: A string including address_number and street. These values can also be provided as separate parameters `address_number` and `street`. Sent in the request query. |
| `address-number` | `--address-number ADDRESS_NUMBER` | no | string |  | Structured input: The number associated with the house. Sent in the request query. |
| `autocomplete` | `--autocomplete` | no | boolean |  | Specify whether to return autocomplete results (`true`, default) or not (`false`). Sent in the request query. |
| `bbox` | `--bbox BBOX` | no | string |  | Limit results to only those contained within the supplied bounding box. Sent in the request query. |
| `block` | `--block BLOCK` | no | string |  | Structured input: In some countries like Japan, the block is a component in the address. Sent in the request query. |
| `country` | `--country COUNTRY` | no | string |  | Limit results to one or more countries. Permitted values are [ISO 3166 alpha 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) country codes separated by commas. Sent in the request query. |
| `entrances` | `--entrances` | no | boolean |  | Specify whether to return building entrance data (`true`) or not (`false`, default). Sent in the request query. |
| `format` | `--format FORMAT` | no | string | `geojson`, `v5` | Specify the desired response format of results (`geojson`, default) or for backwards compatibility (`v5`). Sent in the request query. |
| `language` | `--language LANGUAGE` | no | string |  | Set the language of the text supplied in responses. Sent in the request query. |
| `limit` | `--limit LIMIT` | no | integer |  | Specify the maximum number of results to return. The default is `5` and the maximum supported is `10`. Sent in the request query. |
| `locality` | `--locality LOCALITY` | no | string |  | Structured input: Official sub-city features present in countries where such an additional administrative layer is used in postal addressing. Sent in the request query. |
| `neighborhood` | `--neighborhood NEIGHBORHOOD` | no | string |  | Structured input: Colloquial sub-city features often referred to in local parlance. Not available for reverse geocoding requests. Sent in the request query. |
| `permanent` | `--permanent` | no | boolean |  | Specify whether you intend to store the results of the query (`true`) or not (`false`, default). Sent in the request query. |
| `place` | `--place PLACE` | no | string |  | Structured input: Typically these are cities, villages, municipalities, etc. Sent in the request query. |
| `postcode` | `--postcode POSTCODE` | no | string |  | Structured input: Postal codes used in country-specific national addressing systems. Sent in the request query. |
| `proximity` | `--proximity PROXIMITY` | no | string |  | Bias the response to favor results that are closer to this location. Provided as two comma-separated coordinates in `longitude,latitude` order, or the string `ip` to bias based on reverse IP lookup. Sent in the request query. |
| `q` | `--q Q` | no | string |  | The feature you're trying to look up. Sent in the request query. |
| `region` | `--region REGION` | no | string |  | Structured input: Top-level sub-national administrative features, such as states in the United States or provinces in Canada or China. Sent in the request query. |
| `street` | `--street STREET` | no | string |  | Structured input: The name of the street in the address. Sent in the request query. |
| `types` | `--types TYPES` | no | string | `country`, `region`, `postcode`, `district`, `place`, `locality` (+5 more) | Filter results to include only a subset (one or more) of the available feature types. Sent in the request query. |
| `worldview` | `--worldview WORLDVIEW` | no | string | `ar`, `cn`, `in`, `jp`, `ma`, `rs` (+3 more) | Returns features that are defined differently by audiences that belong to various regional, cultural, or political groups. If `worldview` is not set, the `us` worldview boundaries are returned by default. Sent in the request query. |

```sh
mapbox geocoder forward
```

### mapbox geocoder reverse

Reverse geocoding

The **reverse geocoding** query type allows you to look up a pair of coordinates and returns the geographic features there, including a standardized address or place and full geographic context.

`GET https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/reverse`

| Argument | Written as | Required | Type | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `country` | `--country COUNTRY` | no | string |  | Limit results to one or more countries. Permitted values are [ISO 3166 alpha 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) country codes separated by commas. Sent in the request query. |
| `language` | `--language LANGUAGE` | no | string |  | Set the language of the text supplied in responses. Sent in the request query. |
| `latitude` | `--latitude LATITUDE` | yes | number |  | The `latitude` decimal value from the geographic coordinate for the location being queried. Sent in the request query. |
| `limit` | `--limit LIMIT` | no | integer |  | Specify the maximum number of results to return. The default is `1` and the maximum supported is `5`. Sent in the request query. |
| `longitude` | `--longitude LONGITUDE` | yes | number |  | The `longitude` decimal value from the geographic coordinate for the location being queried. Sent in the request query. |
| `permanent` | `--permanent` | no | boolean |  | Specify whether you intend to store the results of the query (`true`) or not (`false`, default). Sent in the request query. |
| `types` | `--types TYPES` | no | string | `country`, `region`, `postcode`, `district`, `place`, `locality` (+5 more) | Filter results to include only a subset (one or more) of the available feature types. Sent in the request query. |
| `worldview` | `--worldview WORLDVIEW` | no | string | `ar`, `cn`, `in`, `jp`, `ma`, `rs` (+3 more) | Returns features that are defined differently by audiences that belong to various regional, cultural, or political groups. If `worldview` is not set, the `us` worldview boundaries are returned by default. Sent in the request query. |

```sh
mapbox geocoder reverse --latitude 0 --longitude 0
```
